sources.title: Hamburg history project: A short history of the city
sources.note: Direct/indexed academic and institutional Hamburg history project. Free-city government, French period, restoration, 1860 reform and incorporation into German Empire. Imported 1715 to 1878 is map coverage, not founding/fall.

sources.title: Birgit Steinke: Restoration, revolution and reform in Hamburg
sources.note: Direct full academic educational synthesis: 1815 German Confederation, restoration of earlier order and gates/tolls. Its mistaken numerical description of Senate composition is not used; constitutional passage instead uses Udo Schäfer and original Article 6.

sources.title: Udo Schäfer: The Hamburg constitution of 1860, a milestone of constitutional change
sources.note: Direct 34-page Hamburg University Press chapter. Printed page 160, PDF index 21, reproduces Article 6: Die höchste Staatsgewalt steht dem Senate und der Bürgerschaft gemeinschaftlich zu. Pages 160 to 161 give franchise/property divisions. Historical spelling preserved; no claim of universal suffrage.

sources.title: Historic Museums Hamburg: The Grocers’ Guild Widows’ Apartment
sources.note: Direct collection-building account. Houses 1676, twenty widows, nineteenth-century use, reconstructed museum furnishing from other grocers’ homes. Kitchen interior window, alcove bed, fuel loft, courtyard shared toilet, two pumps until late nineteenth-century pipes. All three passages combined below 200 words.

sources.title: Stiftung Wasserkunst: The Great Fire and the city waterworks
sources.note: Direct waterworks heritage institution: fire 5 to 8 May 1842, deficient firefighting water, reconstruction and 1848 waterworks. Avoid inconsistent proportion of city destroyed across other accounts.

sources.title: Hamburg Wasser: History of Hamburg’s water supply and drainage
sources.note: Direct institutional utility history: William Lindley, gravity sewer, first Siel 1843, Rothenburgsort waterworks 1848, hydrants. No claim that every household immediately connected.

sources.title: Hamburg Wasser: The Kaltehofe waterworks
sources.note: Direct utility history: centralized supply 1848, filtered drinking water beginning with Kaltehofe 1893. Later improvement explicitly after map interval.

sources.title: Kirsten Heinsohn: Women’s movements in nineteenth-century Hamburg
sources.note: Direct historian’s article: Paulsen association childcare and poor girls’ school; institutions united as Paulsenstift 1866; Johanna Goldschmidt’s Fröbel association 1860 and professional kindergarten training. Do not repeat conflicting 1865/1867 association date.

sources.title: Johanna Meyer-Lenz: Hamburg’s development into a modern overseas port
sources.note: Direct scholarly synthesis: Sandtorhafen completed 1866, quays, sheds, rail connection, cranes and specialized labor. Another overview says 1867 inauguration; prose uses mid-1860s to avoid equating construction and opening dates.

sources.title: Hamburg Gasnetz archive: Energy supply before 1887, contemporary report excerpt
sources.note: Direct four-page source worksheet transcribing 1887 municipal infrastructure account supplied by Gasnetz Hamburg historical archive. PDF page 1 lines 19 to 23: 1845 trial interrupted by storm-flood damage, regular lighting 5 September 1846, 2020 lamps at year end. Original retrospective report distinguished from modern invention.

sources.title: Hartmut Müller, Bremen State Archive: The city’s road to independence
sources.note: Direct archive-authored history: 1646 imperial recognition, 1741 Stade settlement, French annexation decision 1810/restoration 1813, 1815 Confederation, 1827 port acquisition, 1867 and 1871 federal transformations. Budget includes overview, summary and ending.

sources.title: Bremen Senate: Bremen chronology
sources.note: Direct official PDF chronology, page 3: 1806 free-city title, 1810 annexation, 1815 Confederation; page 4 nineteenth-century changes. Decision 1810 is not confused with administrative implementation in 1811.

sources.title: Bremen Senate: Julius Gottlob von Nostitz and the reversal of constitutional reform
sources.note: Direct official historical reassessment: 1848/49 male citizens at least 25, 1849 constitution, 1854 rollback of equal male-citizen suffrage and stronger Senate. Clearly citizenship restriction and female exclusion remain.

sources.title: German Emigration Center: A print of the emigrants’ house, circa 1850
sources.note: Direct museum object account. April 1850 opening; capacity up to 2000, steam kitchen 3500 portions, nine dormitories with bunks for three/four, washing rooms and medical rooms. 1862 rail changed demand; 1865 closure. Counts are capacities, not continuous occupancy.

sources.title: Focke Museum: Rural life in the Bremen region
sources.note: Direct building collection: Mittelsbüren house 1586 or 1587, continued until relocation; Tarmstedt barn inscribed 1803, outside Bremen itself and moved later. Rural work includes flax, fishing, dairying, grain, peat and bees.

sources.title: Focke Museum: Light and warmth in the Mittelsbüren farmhouse
sources.note: Direct museum interpretation of surviving farmhouse: open hall, Flett hearth, later separate living/sleeping/kitchen area. Do not assign exact dates to all displayed later utensils.

sources.title: Alfred Löhr, Focke Museum: The physionotrace portrait
sources.note: Direct object study from 2021, body beginning Von Dr. Alfred Löhr (unrelated Rilke material precedes it on current site). Johann Smidt Paris April 1811, tracing mechanism, later reduced print, dissatisfaction and 1814 second portrait; thirteen known Bremen sitters.

sources.title: Bremen School Museum: Research into the city’s school history
sources.note: Direct museum research account: introduction of state compulsory schooling in 1844; collection of schoolbooks, teaching equipment and records. No 1900 classroom details retrojected into 1844.

sources.title: Bremen Heritage Office: The Stadtwerder water tower
sources.note: Direct heritage account under Wasserturm auf dem Werder: 1864 plan, 47-meter tower, completion 1873, two corner turrets chimneys, one stairs, one supply pipes; nineteenth-century technical functions distinct from later reuse.

sources.title: Bremen State and University Library: Senate ordinances and proclamations, 1849 volume
sources.note: Direct catalogue and scanned primary volume link. Attested title Sammlung der Verordnungen und Proclame des Senats der Freien Hansestadt Bremen. Sample quotes opening six words as catalogued, translation supplied; preserve historical Proclame spelling. Series catalogue explains publication year differs from reported year, so no assumption that every item dates 1849.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Imported 1715 to 1878, core-city bbox 9.7507,53.4545 to 10.1179,53.6947. Regional display is not full historical territory; entry foregrounds eighteenth/nineteenth centuries, not medieval Hanse only. French interruption explicit; periods do not imply uninterrupted sovereignty. Kramer houses founded earlier but used in this interval; later 1893 filtration explicitly beyond map. Sandtorhafen mid-1860s avoids competing completion/inauguration years. No current museum prices or opening claims used.

Imported 1715 to 1878, core-city bbox 8.5591,53.0260 to 8.7427,53.1675. Public overview flags omission of Bremerhaven and incomplete lifetime. City-state narrative not confused with surrounding Duchy of Bremen. Annexation decision dated 1810, restoration 1813 per archive; implementation in 1811 is not contradicted. Farmhouse earlier construction explicitly labeled with later continued use. No late nineteenth-century classroom equipment retrojected. SWB popular account was not used because it misdates Hamburg cholera to 1902; tower functions use heritage authority.
